newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks tumble again, more downside forecast.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks tumble again, more downside forecast.

text.p: Thailand's battered stock index tumbled to a fresh 5-1/2 year low on Wednesday as a host of lingering worries sparked further sales and analysts said the market's outlook remained bleak.
The composite Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index continued to defy the buoyant tone of other Asian markets on Wednesday, falling another 2.60 percent to 626.57 points.

Although record highs in U.S. and British stocks have boosted most regional markets in recent days, Thai stocks have been pummeled and are now nearly 53 percent lower than the SET close exactly one year ago when it stood at 1,319.20.
Selling on Tuesday had already pulled the SET down to its lowest close since November 1, 1991.
Economic concerns underpin the current slide, analysts said.
"This doesn't look like it is going to be a good year for the Thai economy," said Somchai Trairattanapirom, vice president at Sitca Investment and Securities.

"From an optimistic view perhaps the SET index can stand above 600 but since we have to follow the Bank of Thailand's (economic) indicators, they don't give us such a good picture and it is possible the market will go below 600," he said.
The lower economic growth prospects and reduced expectations of a strong and imminent recovery also sparked blue chip sales, traders said.
Banks stocks shed 2.94 percent, commerce 3.53 percent, and energy 2.53 percent. Telecommunications stocks, hit by slow business growth and industry liberalisation, fell 3.34 percent.
Property firms, hit by a market glut, declining asset values, and liquidity problems, saw share prices fall 4.70 percent.
Renewed concerns over loan quality hit finance and securities stocks, which dropped 3.93 percent, traders said.
The Bank of Thailand has ordered firms to disclose their level of non-performing assets by June 30 and investors are increasingly worried about the figures, traders said.
"I think investors are scared about the level of non-performing loans in the finance sector," said one local trader.

The Thai baht's peg to the U.S. dollar means high domestic interest rates -- minimum lending rates are among the highest in the region at 12.75 percent -- cannot be cut to levels which would strongly stimulate the economy without leaving the currency vulnerable to speculative attack.
The Bank of Thailand and the Finance Ministry have repeatedly placed currency stability at the top of their agenda ahead of economic growth.

The strategy leaves many believing a recovery in the Thai economy, or an export resurgence, may be further away then many commentators expected at the start of the year and offers a bleak outlook for the market.
"Normally you need a catch, something to happen to stop a market like this from falling but I can't see it," said one senior foreign analyst.
